title: Close the gap

predict.q: Real output is 460; full-employment output is 500: a deflationary (recessionary) gap of 40. The government raises spending, and AD shifts right until the gap is closed. What happens?

options.s: Real output rises to 500 and the average price level rises
options.fb: AD moves right along SRAS: the gap closes at output 500, with the price level at 105.

options.s: Real output rises to 500 and the average price level falls
options.fb: AD moves right along an upward-sloping SRAS, so the price level rises, not falls.

options.s: Real output stays at 460: only the average price level rises
options.fb: There is spare capacity (460 < 500), so firms can raise output.

options.s: Real output falls, because the government must borrow the money
options.fb: Borrowing has costs, but the spending itself adds to AD now, so output rises.

task: Move the spending slider and watch AD shift. Find the setting that closes the gap.

target.do: Find the spending boost that closes the gap, then press Check.
target.hint: Keep moving the spending slider until the gap is closed.

takeaway: Expansionary fiscal policy shifts AD right: real output and jobs rise, and so does the price level.
